one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 2.1x fair value. Interesting below about $107.

profile.what: CME Group operates the world's largest futures and options exchanges, including the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX. Its contracts are the benchmarks for US interest rates, stock indices, oil, gold and grains.
profile.money: It charges a fee for every contract traded and cleared, and sells market data. Volumes rise when markets are volatile and when more debt needs hedging. Costs are largely fixed, so margins are very high.
profile.valued: CME is valued on P/E and dividend yield, since it pays out most of its earnings. The stock tends to do well in volatile markets and is watched for new competition in interest-rate futures.

meaning.what_it_does: Runs the largest futures exchanges in the world, for interest rates, stock indices, energy, metals and farm products.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: A fee on every contract traded and cleared, plus market data.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Traders go where the most trading already is, and its clearing house holds their open positions.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: A long period of calm markets, or a serious rival for interest-rate futures.

moat.summary: Liquidity attracts liquidity: each of its main contracts is the dominant market for that risk.

industry.summary: Exchanges and market data change slowly; trading volumes move with market activity.

management.summary: Pays out nearly all its earnings as dividends, including a large annual special dividend.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow: $3.8B a year: free cash flow less stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 2–8% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 66%; cost of capital 8.8%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
